notes: Fiscal year ended 31 March 2025 (Infosys 'fiscal 2025'; matches data.js fy 'Mar 2025'). CURRENCY: the IFRS consolidated statements in the Form 20-F are presented in US dollars ('Dollars in millions'), so the whole record is in USD from the 20-F. The Indian Integrated Annual Report uses Ind AS in INR (it reports a dividend cash outflow of ₹20,295 crore, excluding dividends paid on treasury shares), but no INR figure is used for cash, workers or geography. OWNERSHIP comes from the Integrated Annual Report 2024-25, because the 20-F's Item 7 table lists only Life Insurance Corporation of India (9.61% at 30 May 2025) and directors and officers as a group (2.46%), and Murthy is not a director or officer. Murthy is listed individually as a promoter with 1,51,45,638 shares (15,145,638), 0.36% of 415,32,63,455 shares at 31 March 2025. FAMILY: the 13.05% 'Promoters & Promoter Group' figure is the disclosed total for all of Infosys's co-founder promoters and their families (Murthy, Nilekani, Gopalakrishnan, Shibulal and Dinesh families). It includes Murthy's own 0.36% and is not Murthy's family alone. Members of Murthy's own family are also listed individually as promoters (Rohan Murty 1.46%, Akshata Murty 0.94%, Sudha N. Murty 0.83%, Ekagrah Rohan Murty 0.04%), but the report gives no total for them, so none is recorded. No promoter is relisted in largestHolders. HOLDERS: from the annual report's list of non-promoter, non-ADR holders above 1% (PAN-based) at 31 March 2025. LIC is India's state-owned life insurer; it is typed 'other' because it invests policyholder funds. The 20-F gives LIC 9.61% at 30 May 2025 (a later date). ADR holders (10.59% as a category) are not a beneficial owner and are excluded. BUYBACKS: none in fiscal 2025 (the cash-flow line shows '—'); the last buyback was in fiscal 2023. DIVIDENDS exclude dividends to non-controlling interests (nil in fiscal 2025). STOCK COMP: $95 million, which rounds to 0.10 billion at two decimals. The same $95 million appears as 'Stock compensation expense' in the cash-flow statement. Grants are made under the 2015 and 2019 (Expanded Stock Ownership) plans to 'eligible employees' and are performance-based, so no broad-based employee plan is recorded.

footprint.notes: The FY2025 20-F (year ended March 31, 2025) gives employees for India (250,553), the Americas (34,388), Europe (20,701) and the rest of the world (17,936). No single-country figure outside India, and no U.S. state breakdown, is given. The annual report PDF on infosys.com returned HTTP 403 to automated requests, so the SEC copy of the 20-F was used. Sites come from the 20-F table of most significant properties (buildings over 500,000 sq ft or land over 440,000 sq ft), in this column order: location, building sq ft, seating capacity, ownership, land sq ft, ownership. The 20-F says Infosys has a presence in 292 locations across 59 countries. The 20-F lists Hyderabad under Andhra Pradesh; it is now in Telangana, so place omits the state.
